messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — SkylineCorp (privnet, dedicated pool skyline-dedicated-01): sudden 5xx spike on tenant endpoints, NLB target group health flapping. Severity: P1. Paging net-oncall.

alice_netops: I'm on the pager, joining bridge. @ben_oncall @irene_se can you join?

ben_oncall: on call, joining. Any customer-facing impact?

sam_support: Skyline support reporting ~30% of requests to their /v1/generate endpoints returning 502/504 since ~09:10 UTC. Customer impact: degraded, retries causing increased latency.

irene_se: I can see the Skyline VPC in the console. NLB target group shows ~50% unhealthy targets in az-a and az-b. Target error: TLS handshake resets, connection refused. Recent change: terraform apply by infra-automation ~09:22 UTC.

deploy-bot: terraform: run by infra-automation at 2026-03-17T09:22Z — changed security_group ingress for skyline-app-nodes: tightened from 0.0.0.0/0:443 -> 10.12.0.0/16:443 (run-id: tf-5582).

alice_netops: That looks like it could block NLB healthchecks if the NLB is using ephemeral source IPs. Don't roll back yet — let's validate which source IPs are expected.

ben_oncall: grabbing NLB healthcheck log.
``` 
NLB-health: check from 34.217.11.142 -> port 443, target 10.12.4.21:443 => connection reset
Target status: UNHEALTHY (TLS handshake failed)
```

irene_se: Confirmed. NLB healthchecks originate from AWS-managed IPs that are not in 10.12.0.0/16. The terraform change restricted inbound to the private net. That explains the flapping.

alice_netops: Action plan: 1) Add a temporary SG rule to allow AWS ELB healthcheck CIDR range (0.0.0.0/0 for healthcheck ports) only from NLB -> targets, 2) shift traffic weight to secondary dedicated pool in eu-west-1 (fallback) to reduce customer impact, 3) coordinate with infra-automation for a corrected deploy (restrict but include ELB healthchecks).

irene_se: I can add the SG exception now. Applying minimal change: allow tcp/443 from 34.217.0.0/16 (approx — will use exact prefix list) to skyline-app-nodes.

irene_se: applied SG rule: inbound tcp 443 from 34.217.11.0/24 for target group.

ben_oncall: updating target group healthcheck settings to be forgiving while we stabilize: set healthy threshold 3 -> 5, unhealthy threshold 2 -> 10, interval 10s -> 20s.
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --health-check-interval-seconds 20 --healthy-threshold-count 5 --unhealthy-threshold-count 10
```

alice_netops: Also adjusting Route53 traffic policy: shift 70% traffic to skyline-dedicated-01-standby in eu-west-1 to buy time.

sam_support: I notified Skyline oncall (skyline_oncall) that we have a mitigation in progress and briefly shifted traffic. They acknowledge.

skyline_oncall: Thanks, we see errors dropping from 30% -> 12% on our side. Please keep us posted; we'll pause client retries.

ben_oncall: Conntrack on the nodes is high, likely due to retry storms. Running quick cleanup and lowering system conntrack max to free sockets.
```
sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
sudo conntrack -F
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
```

irene_se: After SG change + conntrack flush + route53 shift, target healthy count improved to 85% within 6m. 5xx rate dropped to ~4%.

alice_netops: Great. Next steps: revert the overly-restrictive terraform change in infra-automation and add an explicit note in their module to allow ELB healthcheck prefixes (or use managed prefix-list). Also update runbook to call this out.

deploy-bot: Created issue infra/TF-780: "Ensure ELB healthcheck prefixes are preserved in skyline-app security group change".

sam_support: Customer notification: sent status update with ETA for permanent fix and offer of post-incident call.

alice_netops: Recommend follow-up postmortem and a small post-change guard: preview security group diffs that remove ELB ranges. Adding to action items.

ben_oncall: handing back to infra rotation. I'm clear on pager. If errors reappear ping me.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> mitigation in place. Monitoring for 30m stabilization window.

alice_netops: closing bridge in 10m if stable. Will open a postmortem doc and link here. Thanks all.
